inspection_summary.note: Texas HHSC inspections, report investigations and assessments since October 2017, updated daily.

occurrences.finding: Policies Comply with Rules: Operational policies were reviewed the following were still observed to be missing:  1.	Days, hours, and months of operation  4.	 Immunization requirements for children, including tuberculosis screening and testing if required by your regional Texas Department of State Health Services or local health authority   5.	Hearing and vision screening requirements   6.	Promotion of indoor and outdoor physical activity that is consistent with Subchapter F of this chapter (relating to Developmental Activities and Activity Plan). Your policies must include: (A) The benefits of physical activity and outdoor play (B) The duration of physical activity at your operation, both indoor and outdoor (C) The type of physical activity (structured and unstructured) that children may engage in at your operation (D) Each setting in which your physical activity program will take place(E) The recommended clothing and footwear that will allow a child to participate freely and safely in physical activities(F) The criteria you will use to determine when extreme weather conditions pose a significant health risk that prohibits or limits outdoor play (G) A plan to ensure physical activity occurs on days when extreme weather conditions prohibit or limit outdoor play.   8.	Instructions on how a parent may access :(A) Minimum standards online; (B) Texas Abuse and Neglect Hotline; and (C) HHSC website.   9.	Preventing and responding to abuse and neglect of children, including: (A) Required annual training for employees  (B) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of issues regarding child abuse and neglect, including warning signs that a child may be a victim of abuse or neglect and factors indicating a child is at risk for abuse or neglect (C) Methods for increasing employee and parent awareness of prevention techniques for child abuse and neglect  (D) Strategies for coordination between the center and appropriate community organizations (E) Actions that the parent of a child who is a victim of abuse or neglect should take to obtain assistance and intervention, including procedures for reporting child abuse or neglect   10.	 Information on vaccine-preventable diseases for employees, unless your center is in the home of the permit holder. The policy must address the requirements outlined in ?746.3611 of this chapter (relating to What must a policy for protecting children from vaccine-preventable diseases include?)  11.	 Procedures for supporting inclusive services to children with special care needs. The policy must address the requirements outlined in ?746.2202 of this chapter (relating to What are my responsibilities when planning activities for a child in care with special care needs?)

Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer: 3 infants were observed to be sitting in wooden chairs and were not strapped in.    NOTE: The wooden chairs were designed with straps. The straps appeared to be worn and were knotted.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Chairs - Safety Straps Used if Required by Manufacturer (26 TAC §746.4501(b))

occurrences.finding: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - No Overlap: Use zone for a slide and track ride were observed to be overlapping.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Measurement of Use Zone for Slides - No Overlap (26 TAC §746.4805(d))

Children's Products- Review list and Remove unsafe products: Two Rock N' Play sleepers recalled 1/9/2023 were observed at the operation. One of which was in use by a 3mo child in care.    NOTE: Operation completed the children's product safety certification 9/6/24. Both sleepers were removed during the inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Children's Products- Review list and Remove unsafe products (26 TAC §746.4135(a))

occurrences.finding: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times: Upon arrival, two children were observed to be eating breakfast and watching TV.    NOTE: The TV was turned off by the caregiver in charge.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Screen Time Activities - Not Used During Eating or Rest Times (26 TAC §746.2207(c)(4))

occurrences.finding: Safety Requirements for Play Yards - Use and Clean According to Manufacturer's Instructions: An extra mattress pad was observed inside one of the play yard. The warning label states not to use extra padding in the play yard.    Note: Pictures were taken for the file. No infants were in the play yard at the time of the inspection. The padding was removed during my inspection.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Safety Requirements for Play Yards - Use and Clean According to Manufacturer's Instructions (26 TAC §746.2411(1))

occurrences.finding: Documented Annual Training- Required Content: The training certificate showing the director has completed the required training topics was not available for review.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: 1 out of 5 children's files evaluated were missing immunizations.

Documented Annual Training- Required Content: 4 out of 5 staff records evaluated did not contain the following training topics:  Emergency Preparedness  Responding to Food Allergies  Handling Storing and Disposing of Hazardous Materials  Understanding Building and Physical Premises Safety  Preventing The Spread of Communicable Diseases
occurrences.violation_type_title: Documented Annual Training- Required Content (26 TAC §746.1309(e))

occurrences.finding: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers: During the inspection an infant was observed sleeping with a pacifier attached to their clothing.    Note: The provider corrected this during the inspecton by removing the pacifier attachment.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Basic Requirements for Infants - Free from Choking Objects That May Cause Choking in Infants or Toddlers (26 TAC §746.2401(6))

occurrences.finding: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days: The feeding instructions for 2 infants have not been signed by parents within the last 30 days.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Written Feeding Instructions - Review and Update Every 30 Days (26 TAC §746.2421(b))

occurrences.finding: Report Number of Employees: A review of the Employees Who Left Employment in 2021data from February 23, 2022, revealed that the center had not reported the number of employees who left employment in 2021by February 22, 2022, as required.
Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness: Operation did not notify licensing on their first case of communicable illness.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Report Outbreak of Communicable Illness (26 TAC §746.305(a)(4))

occurrences.finding: Children's Records - Immunizations: Immunization information was missing on one out of eight files checked.
Required Admission Information - Release Information: Release information was missing on one out of eight files checked.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Required Admission Information - Release Information (26 TAC §746.605(7))

occurrences.finding: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age: There were three torn sleeping mats found in the classroom. They were removed and replaced with the names of the children written on them.
occurrences.violation_type_title: Individual Cot, Bed, or Mat for Each Walking Child Through 4 Years of Age (26 TAC §746.4503(a))
